title: Finite type relation kernels in a coherent cokernel
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and let $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume that $\mathcal F$ is of finite type and $\mathcal G$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For every morphism $f:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, every open $U\subseteq X$, every integer $n\geq0$ and every morphism $g:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to(\operatorname{Coker}f)|_U$, the sheaf $\operatorname{Ker}g$ is of finite type. Here finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections, and the cokernel is taken in the category of module sheaves.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian), proof of (3), cokernel paragraph

proof.text: For each x in U apply the corrected local finite-free replacement, obtaining V_x ≤ U containing x and an epimorphism from kernel ψ_x to the restriction of kernel g. These V_x form a covering family in Over U; on each test open Y use V_x ∩ Y to verify the covering sieve.
The coherence relation condition makes kernel ψ_x finite type. Its epimorphic image, the overMap restriction of kernel g to V_x, is finite type.

Use the private generator-transport lemmas in CoherentKernelConditionRestriction to transport finite type through the iterated-slice equivalence, identifying this restriction with (kernel g).over (Over.mk (V_x → U)). Apply the private finiteType_of_cover lemma in CoherentFiniteTypeSubKernel: combine local generator covers with CoversTop.over and transport their generators through iterated-slice equivalences. This yields finite local generators of kernel g on U.
